summary:
AETHER-4D (Analog Earth-to-Target Heuristic & Environment Ranker) is an interactive, real-time decision-support web platform designed to de-risk Moon and Mars surface missions before launch. Testing off-world hardware in single-variable Earth analogs often leads to costly subsystem failures because planetary environments impose simultaneous thermal, mineralogical, radiation, and logistical stresses.

Grounded in verified NASA planetary datasets and field geology records, AETHER-4D allows mission planners to select target sites -such as Jezero Crater Paleolake or Shackleton Crater Rim- and dynamically adjust priority sliders across four critical dimensions: Thermal & Climate, Mineralogy & Geology, Radiation & Shelter, and Field Access & Logistics. The client-side scoring engine evaluates and ranks eight global Earth analogs (including Lake Salda, Haughton Impact Crater, and Atacama Desert) in milliseconds, replacing fragmented literature reviews with a transparent, repeatable site-selection standard.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

AETHER-4D (Analog Earth-to-Target Heuristic & Environment Ranker) is an interactive decision-support web platform that matches Moon and Mars mission targets with Earth's closest analog environments. Users select an off-world target (such as Jezero Crater Paleolake or Shackleton Crater Rim) and adjust mission priority weights across four critical dimensions: Thermal & Climate Stress, Mineralogy & Geology, Radiation & Terrain Shelter, and Field Access & Logistics. Our real-time weighted scoring engine evaluates and ranks eight global Earth analog sites—including Lake Salda, Haughton Impact Crater, and Atacama Desert—in milliseconds.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

Testing off-world hardware in single-variable analogs often leads to costly subsystem failures. AETHER-4D replaces fragmented literature reviews with a transparent, repeatable 4D heuristic, helping mission planners and engineers de-risk rover and habitat testing before launch.

Tools, Languages & Development:

Built as a lightweight, zero-latency client-side web application using HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript with a modular JSON dataset grounded in verified NASA planetary records and field geology literature. Hosted via GitHub Pages for instant, open-access deployment across desktop and mobile devices.
